stories.notes: Cross-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature with empty acceptance criteria and no prior spec. Complex real-time CMS preview requires openspec to elaborate ACs and technical scope first, then speckit to harden testability, security, and edge cases.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — Live Preview does not exist in the codebase. The central attachment point is useContent, which all 236 content-consuming components flow through. Acceptance criteria were empty; VCs derived from the description alone. Contentstack services are unreachable at test time, so VCs are written to the boundary of what our code sends/receives, not what the external service does.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with a helpful note identifying useContent as the central attachment point and noting that Contentstack services are unreachable at test time. I derived all 17 ACs from the story title, file paths, and Contentstack Live Preview domain knowledge. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 establish the core preview vs. non-preview behavioral fork; (2) AC-9/AC-11/AC-14 address security and performance concerns about preview code leaking into production; (3) AC-6/AC-7/AC-8 cover error handling and resilience for the real-time connection; (4) AC-15 explicitly calls out the cross-codebase consistency requirement including the Metrolinx casing variant; (5) AC-17 addresses the edge case of rapid updates causing performance degradation. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: File contents were unavailable — the criteria are based on file paths and naming conventions only. Reviewing the actual useContent return type, ContentstackContext shape, and contentCard interface could refine AC-3's update timing, AC-10's parameter format, and AC-13's error-state shape.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: All four manifest paths exist (src/hooks/useContent.ts, src/context/ContentstackContext.ts, src/interface/content/contentCard.ts, src/components/contentstack/ContentstackLink/ContentstackLink.tsx) — no missing_manifest_path. Both agents added non-overlapping value: openspec identified useContent as the central attachment point and flagged that Contentstack services are unreachable at test time (important boundary constraint); speckit derived 17 acceptance criteria covering behavioral fork, security/performance leakage, error resilience, cross-codebase consistency (including Metrolinx casing variant), and rapid-update edge cases. However, speckit explicitly states file contents were unavailable and that all criteria are based on file paths and naming conventions only. This is a significant gap: the actual useContent return type, ContentstackContext shape, and contentCard interface were never inspected, meaning AC-3 (update timing), AC-10 (parameter format), and AC-13 (error-state shape) are unverified against real code. For a novel real-time feature touching 236 consuming components, spec grounded in assumptions rather than actual interfaces carries implementation risk. Human review should confirm the derived criteria match the real type shapes before implementation begins.
